text.p: These are the headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Expert witness felt police pressure: Scientist says she was encouraged to overstate her evidence at Morin murder trial.
- Canada, U.S. take steps on smog: Acid-rain watch faces budget cut.
- Ozone level hits new low: Thinning confined to Arctic regions.
- Troops switch sides in Zaire's copper capital: Soldiers in Lubumbashi declare support for rebels.
- Baltic states give Russians cold shoulder: Issue of minority rights has turned into nasty spat with Kremlin for Estonia, Latvia.
- Loons' future threatened by mercury: Airborne poison damages birds' vision and co-ordination, undermines ability to hatch, raise young.
- GM to invest in Quebec plant: Massive spending, adding Catera production would keep Ste-Therese 'viable,' source says.
- Crumbling labs stymie research: Ottawa plans new funding for science, but some members of the research community ask if it will be enough to put Canada back on the right path.
- Bre-X trio took in C$77 million selling shares: Used cheap options to reap big gains.
- Kmart suppliers turn to vultures: Chain's uncertain future spurs trading.
- Kmart suppliers call in vultures: Shaken by Eaton's, Consumers Distributing affairs, some suppliers ask vulture funds to buy their Kmart Canada receivables.
- New Bre-X rumors panic U.S. investors.
